items.title: Beowulf Unlocked: New Evidence from Lexomic Analysis
items.who: M. D. C. Drout, Y. Kisor, L. Smith et al.
items.note: Cluster analysis of vocabulary distribution finds lexically distinct segments, which the authors read as traces of the poet's varied sources rather than multiple authors.

items.title: The Evolution of Verse Structure in Old and Middle English Poetry
items.note: Traces metrical change across alliterative verse and treats Beowulf's meter as representative of an early stage of the tradition.

items.title: The Transmission of Beowulf: Language, Culture, and Scribal Behavior
items.note: Separates scribal modernization and error from the poet's archaic language, arguing the text preserves an early eighth-century composition.

items.title: Communal Creativity in the Making of the 'Beowulf' Manuscript: Towards a History of Reception for the Nowell Codex
items.note: Close study of the two scribes and the codex's making around 1000, relevant to how far the copy reflects a much older exemplar.

items.title: Metrics, Scribes, and Beowulf: A Response to Neidorf (2017), The Transmission of Beowulf
items.note: Critical response questioning parts of Neidorf's metrical reasoning about scribal alteration, a sign the early-date case is still being tested in detail.

items.title: Large-scale quantitative profiling of the Old English verse tradition
items.who: L. Neidorf, M. S. Krieger, M. Yakubek, P. Chaudhuri and J. P. Dexter
items.note: Computational profiling of metrical, lexical and stylistic features across Old English verse finds Beowulf stylistically uniform, supporting single authorship over late compilation.

items.title: Old Norse Influence on the Language of Beowulf: A Reassessment
items.who: L. Neidorf and R. J. Pascual
items.note: Tests each alleged Nordicism proposed by R. Frank and argues all are better explained as archaic features, removing a main linguistic support for a Viking-age date.

items.title: The Nordic Beowulf
items.note: Archaeologist argues the poem's material and social world was created orally in sixth-century Scandinavia, shifting the question toward the age of the underlying tradition.

items.title: Beowulf and the North before the Vikings
items.note: Argues the poem's consistent picture of fifth- and sixth-century northern history is corroborated by archaeology, which sits more easily with early composition.

items.title: The Art and Thought of the Beowulf Poet
items.note: Literary study that reads the poet's ethics and theology against an early eighth-century Anglo-Saxon setting assumed from the linguistic dating.

items.title: Prosody in Medieval English and Norse
items.note: Reanalyses Old English and Norse metre in terms of bimoraism, including a chapter on Kaluza's law in Beowulf, the central metrical argument for an early date.

items.title: Beowulf as a Source Text for Archaic Features
items.venue: The New Cambridge History of the English Language
items.note: Handbook chapter setting out the archaic phonological, morphological and metrical features that underpin the case for composition before about 725.

items.title: Electronic Beowulf, fifth edition
items.note: New edition of the digital facsimile and edition, adding full-word transcript search, metrical analyses and comparison with the Thorkelin transcripts and collations.
